the Sheikh was expecting
that this emir would dismount from his horse,
and come on foot to greet him and kiss his hand, according to custom.
That emir, however, did not dismount,
but only called out a greeting from afar.
And he sent word, saying to the Sheikh:
"Now there is no longer any need for these Tatars to come;
command them to turn back."
And the Sheikh gave permission to the army of the Tatars {OCR: ܥܵܬܵܪܵܝܹܐ} to go.
And when they had gone,
the emir took the Sheikh and those who were with him, and turned off from the road that goes to Birah,
and said:
"We have prepared another place of encampment for you."
And when they went and reached the banks of the Euphrates,
that emir said:
"On the other side we have pitched tents for you."
And the Sheikh replied:
"Wherever you lodge us, we will lodge."
Now as for the Mardin people who had come in the service of the Sheikh,
when they wished to turn back from the Euphrates according to the command of their lord,
the emir of the ruler of Egypt did not let them,
and said to them:
"Our Sultan has commanded that you should come as far as Aleppo."
And so, against their will,
they also crossed the Euphrates,
and they all encamped there.
And at evening time, that emir served abundant foods to the Sheikh and to all those who were with him.
And when they had supped, rested, and slept for about an hour or more,
that emir and those who were with him mounted,
and he sent word, saying to the Sheikh:
"Arise, mount, that we may go."
And the Sheikh contended and said:
"I will not mount
except by day, when the sun rises."
And the emir replied:
"I have been commanded to convey you only by night,
whether you will or whether you will not."
And the Sheikh was angry and said:
"Even if you were to kill me, I will not travel by night."
And the emir said:
"I will not kill you,
but in fetters I will convey you."
And when the Sheikh saw that they intended to demean his honor,
he yielded, arose, and mounted.
And they began to go all night {OCR: ܠܸܓܝܵܐ};
and at early dawn they would dismount off the road,
and far from inhabited places.
And when they reached Aleppo by night,
they lodged him in one of the colleges {OCR: ܒܵܬܲܝ̈ ܕܪܵܫܵܐ}.
And an order came from Alfi, the ruler of Egypt,
that to each one of the Mardin people who had come in the service of the Sheikh they should give two hundred zuzē,
and send them back to their country;
but him, the Sheikh, and his companions,
and the Mongol emir who was with him,
and Shams al-Dīn, the envoy of the lord of Mardin,
they should bring with caution
